prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This manifesto proposes policy changes across public services, the economy, rights, the environment, and international affairs. Key measures include:

Health
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals, and adding 10,000 beds; a £1,000 average pay rise for the lowest‑paid NHS staff.
- Abolish charges for dental and eye checks; invest more in diagnostics; restore NHS dental access.
- Provide state‑funded personal care for long‑term needs; create a Pharmaceutical Agency to end “postcode” variation and reduce drug costs; work toward scrapping prescription charges over time.
- Patient care guarantees, stronger local accountability, independent advocacy, no‑fault compensation, end mixed wards, and ban age discrimination in care.
- Public health focus on pollution and fuel poverty reduction.

Education, Skills and Work
- Invest about £3bn/year (funded by +1p on basic income tax) to reduce primary class sizes to an average of 25; recruit 5,000 secondary teachers; add 40,000 classroom assistants; paid preparation time for primary teachers; trainee salaries; improve ICT, books, and equipment.
- Replace performance‑related pay with progression linked to professional development; reduce testing at age 7; streamline inspections and cut bureaucracy; introduce a flexible minimum curriculum.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorer students; raise loan repayment threshold to £13,000.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 2/3); simplify funding bodies; training incentives for SMEs; paid study leave for 16–24s; replace existing job schemes with a flexible, single Benefits and Jobs Agency.

Policing and Justice
- Recruit 6,000 more police officers; 2,000 part‑time retained community officers; create Community Safety Forces for low‑level disorder.
- Independent police complaints system; evidence‑based stop and search; Europol cooperation.
- Shift from prison expansion toward prevention, work, education, drug treatment, and resettlement; expand community sentences.
- Stronger victims’ rights in court; tackle hate crime; retain jury trials; end most mandatory sentences; youth justice focused on rehabilitation.

Transport
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners and disabled people; aim half‑price fares for under‑19s in full‑time education.
- Abolish vehicle tax for the cleanest vehicles; no real‑terms rise in per‑litre fuel duty in the next Parliament.
- Stronger public control and integration via a Sustainable Transport Authority; restructure rail industry toward public‑interest models; bond‑funded London Underground upgrades.
- Enable local congestion charging and bonds; expand light rail, buses, cycling, walking; rural transport fund; target a 40% cut in road deaths/serious injuries by 2010.

Pensions, Wages, and Benefits
- Increase the basic state pension, with larger rises for over‑75s and over‑80s; create an Independent Pensions Authority; relax private annuity rules; long‑term universal basic pension entitlement.
- Annual review and equalisation of the minimum wage for all 16+; reduce taxes on the lowest incomes over time; extra support for long‑term low‑income families; reform child maintenance; improve housing and disability support.

Business, Consumers, and Environment
- Reduce red tape; £1,500 small business rates allowance; stronger competition and consumer protections; tighter bank regulation; universal Post Office access.
- Replace the Climate Change Levy with a carbon tax; 10% renewable energy by 2010 rising 1% annually; phase out nuclear as stations retire; expand research funding focused on clean technologies.

Governance and Rights
- Fairer voting (AV+ referendum for Westminster; STV for local/European), votes at 16, elected second chamber, stronger committees and FOI, Civil Service Act, long‑term written constitution.
- Deeper devolution to nations, English regions (by referenda), and local government; replace Council Tax with local income tax.
- Equality Act covering multiple grounds; stronger privacy and surveillance safeguards; no ID cards; faster, fairer asylum system with humane support.

Communities, Housing, and Rural Affairs
- Doorstep recycling nationwide; 60% household recycling in 10 years; flood defence overhaul; GM crop moratorium pending evidence; marine protected areas (10%).
- CAP/CFP reforms for sustainability and local management; support for organic and tenant farmers; new Ministry for Rural Affairs.
- Brownfield‑first development, lower VAT on renovation, social housing requirements, action on empty homes, local planning control over phone masts.

Europe, Foreign Policy, Defence, and Development
- EU reform with a constitution clarifying powers, more transparency, subsidiarity, and enlargement; stronger parliamentary scrutiny.
- Maintain defence spending; modern, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing disarmament; oppose missile defence.
- End subsidies for arms exports; strengthen the UN, ICC, and peacekeeping capacity; target 0.7% of national income for aid; debt relief; focus aid on women and HIV/AIDS.
- Enable euro entry at a sustainable rate via referendum; strengthen Bank of England independence; clearer tax/spending transparency; green tax reform.
